story.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

facts.text: The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages.
Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform.
Users can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.
Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.
Did you know that live chat agents on websites can see everything — even messages you never actually sent?
It’s all thanks to a feature known as live typing preview, or real-time typing view, which exists under one name or another in almost every popular customer chat platform.

Here’s how the developer of LiveAgent, a customer support system used by more than 40 000 companies, describes it in its blog: “This live chat typing preview allows agents to anticipate questions and deliver faster responses.
On top of that, users rarely realize an agent can read their message before it’s actually sent.
As an alternative, you can run a quick test: type out a message in the chat box, wait 15 seconds, and see if the agent starts typing a response.
Most importantly, never type personal information into a chat box — even if you are doing so from a Kaspersky Premium device.
Virtually every website selling products or services features a live chat widget.
Google announced its “agentic era” for Google Gemini back in spring 2025, while Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, and the other big players in the AI space have each announced their own AI agents.
The benefit is that once you get over the learning curve, you can customize your AI agent to do what you want.
In any case, of the ones listed above, I think Agent.ai is arguably the best one for beginners.
